extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology using paper XML/PDF text, figures, and recovered supplementary PDF.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptides 5L-8L directly perturb the E. faecium C68 membrane, with depolarization, Laurdan fluidity changes, propidium iodide permeation, growth inhibition, and ATP leakage assays supporting membrane disruption.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact point values are figure-derived and not fully tabulated; the qualitative membrane-disruption mechanism is directly assayed.

source_locator.source_context: Main text and Figure 2 mechanism assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: 5L and 6L show antibiofilm and antipersister activity against E. faecium, including reduced biofilm biomass/live cells and persister-cell killing.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Antibiofilm and antipersister evidence is phenotype-level and should not be normalized to a single molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sub-MIC 5L and 6L downregulate biofilm-associated genes, including ace and ebp-family genes, supporting antibiofilm context rather than a direct binding target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Gene-expression change is indirect mechanism/context evidence.

source_locator.source_context: Biofilm gene qPCR result text and Figure 1H.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MD simulation and metabolomics provide supportive context for 5L membrane insertion and altered metabolism but are not promoted to standalone direct antimicrobial mechanism claims.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational and metabolomics findings are context only; they do not establish a direct cellular target.

source_locator.source_context: MD and metabolomics sections plus recovered supplement tables.
